result.topic_en: Euler reduces the squared algebraic integral of dx/√X = dy/√Y (X a cubic polynomial in xx) to a simpler form, fixes the constant by the condition x = k when y = 0, and begins the special case B = 0, in which that normalisation fails.
result.transcription:
) 56 (
quae ſumtis quadratis reducetur ad iſtam formam:
$\frac{xxX+yyY\mp 2xy\sqrt{XY}}{(xx-yy)^2}=\Delta+D(xx+yy)$
$+E(xx+yy)^2.$
Eſt vero
$xxX+yyY=B(xx+yy)+C(x^4+y^4)$
$+D(x^6+y^6)+E(x^8+y^8)$
hincque peruenietur ad hanc aequationem
$\frac{B(xx+yy)+C(x^4+y^4)+Dxxyy(xx+yy)+2Ex^4y^4\mp 2xy\sqrt{XY}}{(xx-yy)^2}=\Delta.$
§. 77. Sumamus nunc vt ſupra conſtantem $\Delta$ ita vt poſito
$y=0$ fiat $x=k$, et $X=K=B+Ckk+Dk^4\;Ek^6$ [?]
et aequatio integralis induet hanc formam:
$\frac{B(xx+yy)+C(x^4+y^4)+Dxxyy(xx+yy)+2Ex^4y^4\mp 2xy\sqrt{XY}}{(xx-yy)^2}=$
$\frac{B+Ckk}{kk}$, quae aliquanto ſimplicior euadit ſi vtrinque ſubtrahamus C: erit enim
$\frac{B(xx+yy)+2Cxxyy+Dxxyy(xx+yy)+2Ex^4y^4\mp 2xy\sqrt{XY}}{(x^2-y^2)^2}=\frac{B}{kk}$
quae egregie conuenit cum integrali ſupra §. 72. exhibito.
§. 78. Hic caſus notatu dignus ſe offert, dum $B=0$,
tum autem aequatio differentialis ita ſe habebit:
$\frac{dx}{x\sqrt{(C+Dxx+Ex^4)}}\pm\frac{dy}{y\sqrt{(C+Dyy+Ey^4)}}=0$
cuius ergo integrale per conſtantem $\Delta$ expreſſum erit
$\frac{C(x^4+y^4)+Dxxyy(xx+yy)+2Ex^4y^4\mp 2xy\sqrt{XY}}{(xx-yy)^2}=\Delta.$
Hoc autem caſu integratio non ita determinari poteſt, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$; quia integrale poſterioris membri hoc caſu manifeſto abit in infinitum; quam obrem alio

items.english: which agrees excellently with the integral exhibited above in §. 72.

items.english: In this case, however, the integration cannot be determined so that x = k when y = 0, because the integral of the second member here obviously goes off to infinity.
